nodes.characterization_summary: In situ SEIRAS on Pt during HER/HOR (1.1 to -0.3 V_RHE, ref at 1.1 V_RHE = PZC) shows potential-dependent OH stretching (3600-3200 cm⁻¹) and HOH bending (1700-1600 cm⁻¹). At 0 V_RHE, deconvolution reveals weakly H-bonded water (3570 cm⁻¹), asymmetric H-bonded (3450 cm⁻¹, water-cation), symmetric H-bonded (3270 cm⁻¹, ice-like) water. Weakly H-bonded fraction increases LiOH < KOH < CsOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 6a-c shows the OH stretching features of in situ SEIRAS spectra measured... The OH stretching peaks were further deconvoluted into three components: weakly H-bonded water at 3570 cm⁻¹, asymmetric H-bonded water molecules at 3450 cm⁻¹..., and 3270 cm⁻¹... At a given potential, such as 0 V_RHE, the relative peak fraction of weakly H-bonded water at the interface was shown to increase in the order from Li⁺ to K⁺ to Cs⁺.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV measurements on polycrystalline Pt RDE reveal H/OH exchange peaks at ~0.25 V_RHE (Pt(110)) and ~0.32 V_RHE (Pt(100)), with peak potentials increasing with pH from 1 to 14 but showing weak cation dependence.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The peak potentials were extracted from CV measured in Ar-saturated electrolytes on polycrystalline Pt... where the peaks at ∼0.25 and ∼0.32 V_RHE correspond to the potentials of the H desorption peak at Pt(110) and Pt(100) facets.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP analysis confirms the purity of cesium hydroxide electrolyte used with Pt catalyst (see Table S2).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The purity of cesium hydroxide was further analyzed by inductively coupled plasma (Table S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: Classical MD simulations of Pt(111)|electrolyte interface show cation-dependent solvation: structure-breaking cations (Cs⁺, Rb⁺) partially desolvate and segregate to surface at 2.8 Å, while structure-making cations (Li⁺, Na⁺) retain solvation shells at ~4 Å. Peak intensity increases Cs⁺ > Rb⁺ > K⁺ > Na⁺ > Li⁺, more pronounced at pH 13 than pH 1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The z-axial probability distribution functions (ZDF) for surface cations from classical MD simulations for pH1 (Figure 1c) and pH13 (Figure 1d) revealed increasing peak intensity in the order of Li⁺ < Na⁺ < K⁺ < Rb⁺ < Cs⁺... peak center for larger cations such as Cs⁺ and Rb⁺ was found to be 2.8 Å compared to ∼4 Å for that of smaller cations such as Li⁺ and Na⁺.
